source.title: Synaptic Mechanisms of Memory Consolidation during Sleep Slow Oscillations

confidence_rationale: Strong, mechanistically explicit thalamocortical model directly showing that SWS slow oscillations + STDP convert hippocampal ripple input into PREFERENTIAL replay and persistent strengthening of specific cortical sequences. This is the substrate that MECH-120 invokes for the diversity-erosion arm of Q-055. Confidence held below 0.7 because it is a simulation (not behaviour), it does not measure diversity across a population of distinct trajectory classes, and 'preferential strengthening of one trace' does not by itself establish net erosion of the others.
failure_signatures: Hippocampal ripple input delivered during the slow oscillation produces input-SPECIFIC, persistent synaptic potentiation that biases subsequent replay toward the stimulated sequence -- the mechanistic basis for a winner-take-all drift if one trajectory class dominates the ripple input.
The model strengthens whichever sequence the ripple input carries; it provides no intrinsic mechanism that protects under-represented sequences from relative weakening.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Interaction between slow cortical oscillations, hippocampal sharp-wave-ripple input, and spike-timing-dependent plasticity during deep sleep maps hippocampal memory traces to persistent cortical representations via PREFERENTIAL replay of specific cortical spike sequences.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the candidate substrate for the Q-055 erosion arm: if SD-017 SWS replay preferentially strengthens whichever trajectory classes dominate the ripple input (typically the most-recently or most-heavily-weighted ones, per MECH-120), then ARC-065's waking-generated trajectory-class diversity could be systematically narrowed across a sleep cycle.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The model studies strengthening of a single trained sequence, not the comparative fate of a DIVERSE population of trajectory classes. 'Preferential' here is relative to untrained noise, not relative to a set of co-existing learned behaviours. It demonstrates the strengthening mechanism but does not measure diversity loss, and says nothing about ARC-065's waking re-seeding (counter-mechanism a) or designed stochastic sampling in replay (counter-mechanism b).
mapping.source_context: Computational thalamocortical network model with STDP; in silico, mammalian cortical architecture.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality, widely-cited model from the Bazhenov group. Mapping fidelity limited by the single-trace framing vs Q-055's population-diversity framing; transfer risk moderate (in-silico cortical model -> REE trajectory-class diversity).
